subject: Post-demo: adaptive prefix cache economics & pilot plan for Omega Analytics
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@omega-analytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Quick post-demo recap + caching assumptions we discussed

Samir — thanks again for taking the demo yesterday. Short recap and a couple of asks so we can put together a tailored pilot + quote.

Key points from demo (tl;dr):
- Primary workload: customer support assistant + triage for internal ops (short multi-turn chats, lots of repeated prompts across sessions).
- Target SLA: p95 latency < 450ms for 500 token completions.
- Conservation: you want to understand realistic $/1M tokens for production once we apply prefix/session caching and warm layers.

What I promised on the call: a simple sensitivity model for effective $/1M tokens under a few prefix-cache hit-rate scenarios, plus a proposed 2-week pilot to validate hit rates on your data. Before we finalize the pilot scope, two quick asks you can help with:
1) Budget band — what is the monthly budget range you are comfortable committing to for the initial pilot (ballpark is fine, e.g., $5k–$25k)?
2) Historical sample — can you share ~2 weeks of anonymized request logs (just prompt hashes, timestamps, session ids, token counts) so we can compute likely prefix repetition and expected hit rate? S3 or Drive link works.

Attached is a first-pass sensitivity sheet (redwood-cache-sensitivity-v1.xlsx) — below is a short plain-English summary so it's easy to consume.

Assumptions we used for the quick model:
- Baseline model cost (hosted list price for the current recommended model): $50.00 per 1M input+output tokens (this is the unit inference cost before caching).
- Cache serving & storage overhead: assumed $1.50 per 1M tokens (cost to serve cached prefixes, small but non-zero).
- Effective billed tokens = baseline tokens * (1 - prefix_hit_rate). We model three scenarios: conservative (10% hit), expected (35% hit), optimistic (60% hit).

Quick results (effective cost per 1M tokens):
- Conservative (10% hit): base 50 * (1 - 0.10) + 1.50 = $46.50 per 1M tokens
- Expected (35% hit): base 50 * (1 - 0.35) + 1.50 = $34.75 per 1M tokens
- Optimistic (60% hit): base 50 * (1 - 0.60) + 1.50 = $21.50 per 1M tokens

Notes on the numbers: these are illustrative and intentionally simple — the real model we'll run for you accounts for: prefix length distribution (short prefixes are cheaper to cache), KV cache warm-up behavior, batching improvements, and the split between input vs output tokens.

Proposed next steps (short):
- You share the small anonymized sample logs (Aditya can provide the exact schema).
- We run a 3-day internal analysis to estimate your likely prefix hit curve and return a revised sensitivity sheet.
- Agree a 2-week pilot scope (we suggest 10M tokens of live traffic routed through a caching tier + success metric: achieve >= 35% prefix hit and effective cost <= $35/1M).

I'll follow up with a formal 2-week pilot plan and a suggested Statement of Work once you confirm the budget band.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 415-555-0112

Attachments: omega-demo-recording.mp4 (video); redwood-cache-sensitivity-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Samir Shah <samir@omega-analytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@omega-analytics.com
Date: 2027-10-07T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick post-demo recap + caching assumptions we discussed

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. We like the approach and the three scenarios help a lot. A few quick responses: 
1) Budget — for the pilot we can commit to up to $12k/month (likely closer to $8k). If the pilot shows the expected savings, we'll shift to a larger committed capacity.
2) Logs — I'll get our infra team to scrub and drop a 2-week sample into a secure Drive link (will DM the link to you and Aditya). We can provide session ids + prompt hashes + token counts; no PII will be included.

Two clarifying questions on the sensitivity model: 
- Is the base $50/1M the public hosted list price or your internal cost estimate for that model? (we need to align on which baseline you applied).
- For the cache serving overhead, can you break down the $1.50 (memory vs network vs control plane)?

If you can return a pilot plan by EOD Monday (our procurement wants a simple SOW to review), that will keep things moving.

Best,
Samir Shah
Head of Platform Engineering | Omega Analytics
samir@omega-analytics.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@omega-analytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, procurement@omega-analytics.com
Date: 2027-10-08T14:19:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick post-demo recap + caching assumptions we discussed

Samir — great, thanks for the prompt answers and the budget band. Quick replies inline and I attached a short pilot SOW + a one-page breakdown of the cache overheads.

- Base price: the $50/1M is the public hosted list price for the recommended open model we demoed. For Dedicated/Private deployments we would give a different unit with committed discounts; we'll show both numbers in the quote.
- $1.50 overhead break-down (high level):
  - Cache serving compute (GPU/CPU edge mem): $0.90 per 1M tokens (for high QPS serving of cached prefixes)
  - Storage & retrieval (KV lookups, SSD egress): $0.30 per 1M tokens
  - Control plane & telemetry: $0.30 per 1M tokens
  - Note: those components scale differently — the sheet shows sensitivity if serving cost moves +/- 30%.

Updated sensitivity with your budget in mind: if you target an effective $/1M <= $35, the math implies we need a prefix hit >= ~33% under the $1.50 overhead assumption (we show the algebra in the attached spreadsheet). Our recommended pilot target: hit >= 35% so there's clear headroom.

Pilot SOW (attached pdf) — highlights:
- Duration: 2 weeks live traffic (we provision a caching tier in front of the same model).
- Traffic: we target routing ~10M tokens through the caching tier (you control sampling %)
- Success metrics: >= 35% prefix hit and effective cost <= $35/1M OR a validated technical explanation for why hit rate is lower (then we iterate on prefix extraction heuristics).
- Deliverables: detailed hit-rate curve, per-route token breakdown, updated effective-cost quote, and a recommended rollout plan (canary thresholds + rollback criteria).

Action items & owners:
- Samir / Omega infra: share anonymized log link (due: 2027-10-10)
- Redwood (Aditya): run analysis and return revised sensitivity + pilot config (due: 2027-10-12)
- Procurement (Omega): review SOW and flag any legal questions (due: 2027-10-13)

I'll also include a short note for the procurement team explaining licensing differences between Hosted vs Dedicated (helps with procurement approvals).

Thanks — will follow up once we ingest the logs.

Vanessa

On Fri, Oct 8, 2027 at 09:34 Samir Shah <samir@omega-analytics.com> wrote:
> Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap...

Attachments: pilot-mop-up-plan.pdf; redwood-cache-sensitivity-v1.xlsx (updated breakdown)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-09T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: prep for pilot analysis (notes)

Vanessa / Aditya — internal checklist before we ingest Omega logs: 
- Confirm hashing method: we should match their prompt-hash function to determine identical prefixes (Aditya to confirm).
- Run pre-filter: drop any sessions with >10K tokens (outliers) and remove PII fields per their note.
- Set target extraction window: first 64 tokens as 'prefix' candidate, and also test 128 token window to measure sensitivity.
- Quick perf note: if we see >40% repetition on the 64-token window, optimistic-case economics likely attainable.

I'll prep an analysis notebook and a one-pager describing how we convert repetition -> hit-rate estimate -> effective cost. Planning to start analysis as soon as Samir drops the logs.

-Neha
